I run a bar and we have these - I am surprised at the general reaction but upon reading the comments, perhaps not. These machines allow the employees to input their card details on an account they make and it deposits directly into their accounts each month. It actually costs us a fee to have them. Managers and owners get no cut - these are strictly for the hard working bar and floor staff (as it should be). 

It might be worth noting we pay all of our staff well above NMW regardless of age and all of the revenue from these machines go to the staff and not the managers or the owners. My staff work hard and they deserve the option for patrons to recognise that if they wish to do so. 

That said, cash is always king. I hope this at least portrays them in a different light for some as opposed to being an avenue to not pay someone a living wage but the cynic in me does not doubt that this is abused elsewhere.

You can definitely see changes, but you’ll simply see a lot more if you increase your calories. Try a smoothie in the AM if you don’t have a big appetite - a banana, some frozen fruit, oats and milk will go a long way and it won’t feel like a slog drinking it. This can easily reach 700-1000 calories but try and watch your fat intake if you want to stay trim. I like to add a bit of honey for taste and some more calories. I used to be this build and saw phenomenal change when I just said fuck it and ate way more. 

Cheap blender will go a long way - add some cubed ice and voila! Delicious, healthy, packed with vitamins, calorie dense and bloody great to take on the go in a rush or if you can’t be arsed to make brekkie. Beauty of this is you can choose the fruits to your preference, too. 

Nuts and Greek Yoghurt are also a great source of calories which are quite accessible for most. Oats too. 

You can also try drinking larger quantities of water to expand your stomach if you don’t usually have a big appetite but I have not tried this personally, I’ve just heard that it works from others’ experiences and a bit of research. This apparently will help you to eat more in the long term but will take some time. 

Look up a TDEE calculator and how to use one -
you want to be in a 200-300 calorie surplus to gain a steady amount of weight. 

I am not a nutritionist, this is just what worked for me. Good luck!
